content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] severity=sev2 service=runtime cluster=eu-west-1 nodes:3 model-load-failure type=OOM at model warmup 3999123456

sara: seeing a surge of OOMs during model boot on eu-west-1 pool. paging spikes and one container crashed. i’m oncall, looking now.

mike: linking heap/paging graphs — looks like a cascade starting at 3999123420, mem > 95% then swap thrash.

jin: which model variant? is this the new int4 quant build?

sara: yes, v1.2-int4 pushed as canary to 20% earlier today. only the warmup path fails (oom at deserialization). requests still hitting fallback but latency is up for customers pinned to v1.2.

olivia: @sara can you paste the container logs?

sara: attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:31Z] warmup: loading shard 0
[2026-03-15T18:02:36Z] deserialize: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
[2026-03-15T18:02:36Z] runtime: coredump signal SIGABRT
[2026-03-15T18:02:36Z] gpu0: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
```

mike: cuda error on top of heap OOM — probably memory fragmentation + aggressive batch warmup.

ejva: recommend immediate mitigation: stop further canary warmups and scale down warmup concurrency.

sara: starting handoff to infra runbook. @mike you take lead on node isolation, @jin you take model side.

mike: cordoning node n-eu-23 to prevent new pods: `kubectl cordon n-eu-23`
mike: draining warmup pods: `kubectl -n redwood-system drain n-eu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback detected: route v1.2-int4 -> v1.1-stable at 3999123480 (automated rollback triggered by policy).

jin: throttling warmup task queue on router: set WARMUP_CONCURRENCY=2 for eu-west-1.

pagerduty: paging ops-eng primary oncall sara -> acknowledged.

support-ops: customers A123, B321 are reporting elevated latencies; no 500s seen yet. preparing comms.

olivia: quick check — is prefix /chat or /embed effected?
sara: mainly text-generation endpoints pinned to v1.2. embeddings unaffected.

mike: node n-eu-23 drain completed. seeing reduced swap churn. memory utilization trending down to 70%.

jin: deserialization code path likely allocates a temporary buffer per shard. adding a guard to fail early if mem < 1.5x expected. will patch and retest in staging.

olivia: recommend we set routing fallback to quantized-small model for customers currently pinned to v1.2 for next 2 hours until fix verified. can we do that quickly?

sara: doing manual route override: `redwood route update --region eu-west-1 --model v1.2-int4 --fallback v1.1-quant-small --duration 2h` — applied at 3999123512.

incident-bot: [NOTE] severity decreased to sev3 after automated rollback and node isolation 3999123520

jin: submitting PR with a defensive allocation check and reduced batch size for warmup: PR#4821. will request expedited review.

eva: QA run on staging with int4 warmup at concurrency=1 passed. suggest canary re-test at 1% traffic after fix.

support-ops: drafting customer status: "We saw a model warmup issue affecting a small subset of hosted customers in eu-west-1. We rolled back the canary and isolated the affected nodes; no persistent 5xx errors observed. We're running a patch and will follow up with timelines."

olivia: assign follow-ups:
- mike: follow up on node memory profiling and kernel params (vm.swappiness) — due 2h
- jin: land PR and push canary at 1% — due 1h
- sara: coordinate postmortem and draft customer note — due EOD

sara: handoff to night oncall @eva in 20m. leaving notes in incident doc https://redwood.internal/incidents/3999123456

eva: acknowledged, will monitor until 08:00 UTC. set alert thresholds: mem>85% + swap>20% -> pager.

mike: root cause hypothesis: aggressive concurrent warmup for int4 variant + allocation pattern caused host-side heap OOM which cascaded to CUDA allocation failures during model init.

jin: long-term: add preflight memory estimator and fail fast; consider streaming deserialization to avoid big temporary buffers.

support-ops: closing the immediate customer escalation, will reopen if anomalies return. final status at 3999123620: degraded -> mitigated.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] incident mitigated, postmortem assigned. Reference: INC-2026-0345.
